newsitem.title: USA: NYSE likely to vote to end trade in eighths - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYSE likely to vote to end trade in eighths - paper.

text.p: The board of directors of the New York Stock Exchange will likely vote on Thursday to end its 250-year-old practice of quoting stocks in increments of an eighth of a dollar and go to sixteenths, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted government and industry sources familiar with the plan, which would narrow the markup or spread by NYSE market makers or specialists.
Recent academic studies have shown that investors who own stocks such as AT&T Corp. or General Motors Corp. would reap enormous benefits from smaller price increments on the NYSE.

The exchange has faced competitive pressure to lower spreads or risk losing business, since other U.S. stock markets, including the over-the-counter Nasdaq, have adopted the practice of quoting prices in sixteenths.

The move is also seen as a response to legislation that has been introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives to force Wall Street to start trading stocks in dollars and cents, the way grocery stores price bacon or bread, the sources told the newspaper.
Quoting stocks in sixteenths could slow the legislative momentum for requiring decimals, they said.
